key_insight: MECx uses a bond-informed surrogate energy model to find low-energy ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys more efficiently than direct DFT-driven Monte Carlo.
engineering_relevance: Identifying alloy ordering can help engineers understand local structures that influence mechanical and thermodynamic properties.
method: Select training configurations stratified in bond-count space.
Train surrogate energy models on 100 DFT-labeled configurations per alloy.
Guide Monte Carlo searches and examine ordering, thermal disordering, and diffraction signatures.
evidence_signal: Tests on ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys found lower-energy candidates than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits, with transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested BCC alloys and selected binary subsystems remains unestablished.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
